explanation: The sole of the foot is viewed as the dirtiest part of the body across the Gulf, so deliberately pointing it at someone is read as a strong insult rather than a religious rule. This matters in majlis seating and any formal gathering in Saudi Arabia where people sit on low cushions or face each other directly.
local_tip: Sit with both feet flat on the floor or crossed at the ankles, never pointed toward another person.

also_check.note: The feet are considered the lowest and most impure part of the body, making it a serious insult to point them at someone.
Sitting with soles facing others is disrespectful, particularly in traditional settings.
Showing the soles of your feet is generally neutral and only seems informal in unusually formal settings.
